reading.body:
Capgemini is recorded as a 1967-founded public consulting and technology services firm, with no AI products, MCP servers, or lawsuits in the data.

The only AI-specific detail is a described use at the Rugby World Cup, where AI surfaces match insights in real time for fans. That is an application of AI inside a services engagement, not a product Capgemini sells or a model it built. For a firm of this type, AI capability arrives through client delivery work rather than through owned infrastructure.

Nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power. There is no data center footprint, no power contract, no chip supply, and no capital expenditure figure. The absence is a limit of the record, not evidence that Capgemini has none.

The profile also carries no revenue, headcount, or segment breakdown, so its scale in AI work cannot be judged from this data. The founding year and public-company status are the only structural facts present.

profile_text.body:
Capgemini is a public company founded in 1967, operating in consulting, technology services and digital transformation. On its own site it describes itself as a global leader in those areas, offering an array of integrated services that combine technology with deep sector expertise. The site also highlights work applying AI to live match insights, which it says gives fans a more complete and engaging view of the Rugby World Cup than before.

Beyond that description, the record holds no tracked products, no MCP servers, and no lawsuits involving the company.
